A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same work, with matching methods and shared experiments. However, v3.pdf ends after the references despite repeatedly citing an appendix; v4.pdf includes supplementary Sections 8–13. This limits comparison of the supplementary experiments' history, although their newly available documentation can be assessed.

before.justification: v3 reports original PIE benchmark results, qualitative image-editing comparisons, and fixed-point iteration ablations in Sections 6.2–6.3 and Tables 1–2.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and includes additional comparator results, inversion diagnostics, attention-control investigations, pose-editing scores, and failure examples.

M1.justification: Fixed-point inversion with averaging, velocity compensation, and token-aware AdaLN replacement are retained. The expanded Algorithm 1 explicitly includes prompts, editing branches, feature replacement, and the edited output, consolidating the procedure already described in v3 Sections 4–5.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate PIE and demonstrate diverse rigid and non-rigid text-guided edits. The newly specified pose subset and expanded qualitative galleries remain within the editing coverage already described in v3; no distinct new benchmark or domain is established.

E2.justification: v4 adds the Flux-dev-based RFinv comparator to Table 1 and the corresponding qualitative comparison, now Figure 7. PnP, P2P, MasaCtrl, InsP2P, and InfEdit remain. RFinv is not included in the supplementary pose comparison in Table 3.

E3.justification: The shared settings remain unchanged: 30 inversion steps, three fixed-point iterations, CFG 1/2 for inversion/editing, and 150 ablation images. v4 adds a with/without-averaging control and a diagnostic measuring inversion-versus-reconstruction latent MSE at each timestep. These extend evaluation procedures without establishing a revision to the main benchmark protocol.

E4.justification: v4 adds the averaging diagnostic in Figure 4 and supplies iteration-dependent reconstruction-error curves, a substantially fuller image/text Q/K/V injection investigation, and comparative failure cases in Figures 10–12. These substantially expand inspectable component and failure evidence. Some supplementary investigations were already mentioned in v3, so their inclusion does not establish that they were newly conducted.

E5.justification: Figure 11 newly identifies its generations without invariance control as using the same seed. This adds seed-control information; repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, and significance tests remain unreported.

E6.justification: v4 adds RFinv results, diagnostic and qualitative outcomes, and the pose-subset Table 3, where the proposed method reports CLIP Whole/Edited scores of 26.93/22.87. In shared Table 1, MasaCtrl LPIPS changes from 87.94 to 88.79 and SSIM from 81.33 to 80.76. The proposed method's Table 1 scores and all Table 2 values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The rectified-flow equations, fixed-point update, compensation equations, and feature-mapping definition are retained. v4's displayed DDIM inversion equation makes explicit the rescaling already stated in v3 Section 4.1. No new formal assumptions, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same central claims: faithful and editable two-stage flow inversion, and AdaLN invariance control supporting rigid and non-rigid editing. Additional comparisons and diagnostics support these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly explains averaging through potentially non-monotonic fixed-point iterates. The supplement elaborates component-specific attention behavior and why velocity compensation cannot rescue editing after badly mismatched inversion. These refine the existing interpretation; the principal model-domain and computational limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 more explicitly documents the complete editing procedure. The supplement specifies AdaLN replacement S=1, 30 sampling steps, a 40-image pose subset, and one fixed-point iteration for the displayed failure inversions. These are additional disclosures rather than demonstrated changes to previously stated settings. The project-page destination is unchanged.

R1.justification: Sections 2 and 8 substantially broaden the discussion of flow matching and invariance control. v4 acknowledges closely related DiT editing work by Rout and Wang and contrasts its editing-preservation tradeoffs with theirs, while adding foundational flow-model and adapter literature. This changes research positioning beyond citation renumbering or bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and its narrative sequence are retained. Changes include localized rewrites, before/after terminology, expanded pseudocode, author-role notes, and organized supplementary sections. The separate limitations-and-impact section becomes an unnumbered limitations paragraph, and the brief broad-impact paragraph is removed.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with an internal MM-DiT schematic, and the main comparison figure and table expand for RFinv. v4 adds an averaging display, supplementary diagnostics, failure panels, extensive galleries, and Table 3. Several earlier figures are retained under new numbers; the substantial visual additions exceed those numbering and layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: Relative to the supplied v3, v4 resolves an important evidential gap by providing the previously referenced pose results, detailed attention investigation, and failure examples. Averaging and reconstruction-error diagnostics, a relevant flow-based comparator, and clearer algorithm/settings documentation substantially strengthen empirical support and reproducibility. The improvement concerns the paper's substantiation and completeness; its retained performance scores are unchanged, and statistical uncertainty remains unquantified.
